title: Alternation in regular expressions should not contain empty alternatives
description: An empty alternative in a regular expression alternation (e.g., 'a||b') matches the empty string, which is almost always a mistake. This can lead to unexpected matches and bugs in the code using the regular expression.
message: This regular expression alternation contains an empty alternative, which matches the empty string.
impact: Empty alternatives in regular expressions can cause unexpected matches, leading to bugs and security issues.
recommendation: Remove empty alternatives from regular expression alternations to ensure only intended patterns are matched.

noncompliant.code:
import re
pattern = re.compile(r'a||b')
result = pattern.match('')
noncompliant.description: The pattern 'a||b' contains an empty alternative, so it matches the empty string, which is likely not intended.

compliant.code:
import re
pattern = re.compile(r'a|b')
result = pattern.match('a')
compliant.description: The pattern 'a|b' does not contain any empty alternatives, so it only matches 'a' or 'b'.

why_is_this_an_issue: Empty alternatives in regular expressions are almost always a mistake and can cause the pattern to match the empty string, leading to bugs.
how_to_fix: Review the regular expression and remove any empty alternatives from alternations.
